draft.title: Social, legal and political influences
card: Changes in society, such as tastes, values and the age of the population. A business that ignores them can lose customers.
Laws a business must follow, such as consumer law and work health and safety law. Breaking them can lead to fines or court action.
Government policies and decisions, such as a new tax, a grant or a ban on a product. A government can change them when it changes its priorities.
Each of these is part of the general environment. A business cannot control them, so it must adapt to them.
draft.remember: Society changes what customers want, laws set what a business must do, and government policy can change the rules and costs.

a.q: Shoppers in Perth increasingly want products made without harm to the environment. Mei's cleaning supplies shop starts stocking refillable bottles. Which influence is she responding to?
opts: Legal, a new law she must follow
Social, a change in the age of the population
a.why: Shoppers wanting environmentally friendly products is a change in values, which is a social influence. Nothing in the case says a law or a government policy forced the change, so legal and political are wrong.
a.clue: Who is driving the change: society or government?

b.q: A state government bans single-use plastic straws. Dev, who owns a café in Newcastle, must now buy paper straws, which cost more. What is this an example of?
opts: A political influence that raises his costs
A social influence that lowers his costs
A change in the age of the population
A decision Dev controls inside his business
b.why: The government made a policy decision, so this is a political influence, and it raises his costs. Dev cannot control it, so it is not an internal matter. It did not come from changing tastes in society, so it is not social.
b.clue: Who made the decision that changed his costs?

b.best: A political influence that raises his costs

problems.detail: The clue 'Who is driving the change: society or government?' points straight to the answer (society, so social) and gives it away.
The clue 'Who made the decision that changed his costs?' points straight to the answer (government, so political) and gives it away.

screen.summary: Both answers are correct and no other option is defensible. However, each clue points directly at the right answer, so students would not need to understand the influence to pick it; the clues should be removed or made less revealing.

b.best: A political influence that raises his costs

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one clearly correct answer that matches the card. The straw ban example fits real NSW policy.
